blocks.text: Every monster in Unwritten is a **corrupted page** — a drawing from the artist's book that Chaos twisted into hostile form. That's why they appear **flat and papery**: their two-dimensional look isn't a style choice — it's what they *are*. To defeat one is to **restore its page**. Point at one, or fight it, and its **portrait** shows beside its name.

items: **By biome** — each of the fourteen biomes has creatures of its own, and the biome decides which element most of them carry. See *World & Maps*.

**By level** — every monster has a level, exactly like you do. Its level sets its body — its health, its attack, its defence — and its gear sets how hard it is for that level (see *Its gear is its difficulty* below). Ordinary monsters and elites run from level 1 to 99, and the shadows from 105 to 170. Every place has its own creatures, most of them near one level with the odd weaker or stronger visitor, and a monster lives wherever it belongs — you will meet the same slime in field after field.

**By kind** — most monsters are ordinary. A few in each area are **elites**: stronger than the rest. Stronger still are the fourteen **shadows**, one for each weapon, each with a name of its own and gear at the highest grade — they are meant to take a whole guild to bring down. A monster uses only the skills it has learned, exactly as you do, and for now none has learned any — so no elite or shadow calls helpers to its side yet.

**By element** — a monster's element grows stronger with its kind: ordinary monsters are **level 1**, elites **level 2**, shadows **level 3**. Where a monster lives says what it probably is: the plains are mostly Neutral, the forests and hills Earth, the sea and snow Water, the volcano Fire, and the dark lands overseas Poison, Holy, Dark, Ghost and Undead. The shadows between them carry all ten elements, and a converter only answers the four it comes in — Water, Earth, Fire and Wind (see *Combat Mechanics*).

**By size** — every monster has a size of its own, set by what it is: the smallest, like a mouse or a raccoon, stand about a third of your height and nothing is ever smaller, a bear stands taller than you and a giant squid towers four times your height. Every size falls into one of three groups — **Small, Medium or Large**. A Medium monster stands about as tall as you; a Small one under two-thirds of your height, a Large one more than one and a half times it. A bigger monster also reaches further with its blows — and you reach it from further away. Most ordinary monsters are Small or Medium; most elites are Large; every shadow is exactly your size. Winged monsters — butterflies, bats, birds — fly at about your head height; you click and strike them up there, and they reach you exactly as far as they would on the ground. The size group is also meant to interact with your weapon type (see *Combat Mechanics*).

blocks.text: A monster is not built from a different set of numbers than you are. It has the **same six stats**, grown by the **same formulas**, and — this is the part that matters — it gets the **same number of stat points its level allows**. A level 20 monster is carrying exactly what a level 20 player could have bought. Nothing is inflated behind the scenes and nothing is quietly weakened.

items: **It wears real equipment** — a weapon, a head piece, a body piece, shoes and a garment, the same gear you can wear, in the same slots. Its armour follows what it is — metal for shell, scale, horn or bone, leather for hide, fur or feather, cloth for soft, plant, flame or spirit — and its six stats are spent for the weapon it holds.

**Its gear is its difficulty** — a monster's gear has a **grade** and **folds**, exactly like yours, and neither follows its level. The rarer the thing a monster drops, the higher its grade; the harder it is to find, the more folds. So a low-level monster guarding a Legendary material is far harder than its level says, and a common one in plain gear is not.

**Better gear pays more** — a kill's experience, what a shop pays for the monster's own materials, and the Unsigned a saved character hands you all rise with the monster's gear: **25% more for each grade** above Raw, and **5% more for each fold**.
**It can carry Ring investment** — scaling it on the same soft-cap curve yours uses. A monster with a Ring behind it is a genuinely different fight.
**Its stats are visible in its numbers** — a monster that hits hard has the attack to prove it. There is no hidden multiplier making things tougher.

blocks.text: Because a monster is built like a character, anything a skill can do to you it can do to a monster — and the reverse. A monster can be slowed, shielded, guarded, drained, or pulled off its feet just as you can.
Drops — materials, and sometimes its gear

**One kill in ten, a monster drops one piece of what it wears** — a new copy of one piece picked at random, always **Raw +0** however good the monster's own was. An ordinary monster's piece is Common, Uncommon or Rare; an elite's is always Epic; a shadow's always Legendary (see *Weapons & Equipment*). Besides that it gives up **materials** and **consumables** — never coin. What falls lands on the ground where it died: for 10 seconds only the player who earned the kill can pick it up, then anyone can, and it vanishes after a minute if nobody does.

items: **Materials** — **Temper Dust** and, a tenth as often, **Quench Oil**: more the higher the monster's level and the better its gear; and now and then an **Ink** or a **Salt**. Elites drop ten times as much Temper Dust and Quench Oil, and rarer Inks and Salts; shadows twenty times. No stats of their own; they feed **Crafting & Recycling**.

**Its own material** — every ordinary monster and every elite drops one material that nothing else drops. A shop pays more for it the higher the monster's level and the better the monster's gear, and selling these is how hunting earns Unsigned. Some monsters also carry a second, rarer one with a coloured name. An elite's falls as several separate piles, and auto-loot never takes anything an elite drops.

**Its find** — now and then, the one consumable its element carries: Fire, Water, Earth and Wind monsters drop a **converter** of their own element, every other monster drops its element's **food**. Potions, wings and antidotes are only sold by Tool Dealers.

blocks.text: A beaten monster sometimes turns back into the character the artist really drew on its page — about **3 kills in 20**, for ordinary monsters and elites; a shadow never does. The monster's own drops still fall. The character says a line — for its first 2 seconds an aura shows which kind it is: hearts for one that never fights, stars for an ally, a dark haze for a rebel — and it stays for 30 seconds, doing one of three things:

items: **Some never fight.** They thank you, stay a while and leave — and saving one is the only time a fight itself pays **Unsigned**, and it hands you some of that monster's own material too: more for the helpless (children, the old) and more again for the wealthy (the princess, nobles, sultans). The higher the monster's level and the better its gear, the more Unsigned.
**Some fight beside you** against monsters and rebels, then say goodbye. You cannot hit them, and what they beat counts as yours.

**Some rebel.** Cured of Chaos but choosing to fight, they attack anyone nearby like a monster does. A rebel carries **more and rarer loot** — as if it were one kind stronger — and the experience of the monster it came from. An elite always turns into the same ninja, and every ninja rebels.

blocks.text: Everyone who fights a monster earns points for it: **60** shared by damage dealt, **15** by how long it was chasing you, **15** by healing other players it hurt, **5** for the first hit and **5** for the last. The **experience is split** among everyone by their points, so a healer and whoever holds the monster's attention are paid too. Whoever has the **most points owns the loot** for the first 10 seconds.

Every kill starts a run, shown big on the left of your screen: kill again within **10 seconds** and the run climbs by one; wait longer and the next kill starts it again at 1. Each kill pays **1% more experience for every kill in the run, up to 50%** at a run of 50 — and the Unsigned a saved character pays you grows the same way. Under the run you see your **EXP/h** and **u/h**, what your kills paid over the last 10 minutes. A summon or a training dummy is no part of a run, and walking through a door starts it again.

items: **Elites** are the strongest corrupted pages of an area, and they keep calling ordinary monsters to their side.

**The shadows** are the Fourteen Kashira, turned by the artist's fear — the strongest creatures in the world, levels 105 to 170, one for each weapon, each showing its Kashira's name. Thirteen of them are that fear wearing a champion's shape; the fourteenth, **Veyra, the Last Petal**, always at level 170, is Chaos itself. See **The Whole Story**.
